reason: The ribs should establish the whale’s shape around the keel, giving the rest of the frame somewhere to attach.
expectation: I expect a ribbed frame; it will probably still need bracing to hold its shape.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the brace cord also supports the goal, but I prefer to build the basic frame first.

effect: The ribs are in place, so I can continue assembling the frame.
reaction: A straightforward first step; I'm curious how the frame will be stiffened.
reason: The upper spar should connect and support the ribs before bracing.
expectation: I expect the spar to strengthen the ribbed frame, though it may still need diagonal bracing.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the braces is useful too, but finishing the main frame first seems practical.

effect: The upper spar is fitted, and the tail can now be attached.
reaction: Straightforward progress; the bracing still seems important.
reason: I'll attach the tail while continuing the main frame assembly.
expectation: I expect the frame to gain its whale tail, but still need a deck and bracing.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the braces could help stiffen the frame, but I prefer to attach the tail first.

effect: The tail is attached, and the deck is ready to fit.
reaction: The frame is taking on its whale shape, though the steps have been straightforward.
reason: The deck should provide a surface for the fair and complete more of the frame.
expectation: I expect a decked whale frame that still needs diagonal bracing.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the braces is also useful, but I want to fit the deck first.

effect: The deck is fitted; preparing the bracing is the remaining offered combination.
reaction: The assembly remains straightforward, and I want to see how the bracing works.
reason: I'll prepare the brace cord and tensioners to help the frame keep its shape.
expectation: I expect a tensionable brace assembly that can be fitted to the frame.

effect: The brace cord and tensioners are assembled and ready to fit to the frame.
reaction: I'm interested to see whether the braces explain how the frame resists bending.
reason: Fit the braces to help the whale frame keep its shape; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a stiffened whale frame, with the diagonal braces helping prevent it from skewing.

effect: The braces completed the frame and showed how diagonal cords resist the frame skewing sideways.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the whale hold its shape while remaining open, though the explanation echoed the earlier crane braces.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the diagonal braces was the most worthwhile action: it connected the finished whale shape to a clear structural purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: The consecutive rib, spar and tail fittings felt routine, with little feedback beyond the new frame names.

surprise.text: Nothing particularly surprised me; the brace explanation confirmed what I expected from the earlier crane frame.

arbitrary.text: The tail fitting had a clear visual purpose, but its contribution to the goal of a shape-holding frame was less clear.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see the whale become a flying fair, although I hope the next chapter offers more consequential choices or a new mechanism to explore.
